contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.

As the city transport planner, pick which stretches of roadway to upgrade so that each designated neighborhood cluster is internally connected while keeping the total construction cost as low as possible; clusters do not need to be linked to each other.

As the network operations lead, choose which fiber links to activate so that every listed set of office sites form a continuous communications path, minimizing the aggregate amount spent on links, and different site sets may remain separate.

As the park superintendent, decide which footpaths to build so that each group of trailheads is reachable from any other in the same group while using the least total paving length, and there is no requirement to join different groups.

As the utility planner, select which transmission lines to commission so that each collection of substations is connected for power flow, keeping the sum of line installation costs minimal, and separate collections can stay disconnected.

As the museum curator, determine which corridors to open so that exhibits in each themed cluster are all accessible to one another, while minimizing total renovation expense, and themed clusters need not be connected together.

As the irrigation designer, pick which canals to dig so that every set of targeted fields is connected by water channels, minimizing the total digging length, and different field sets do not have to be joined.

As the telecom project manager, choose which cell backhaul links to build so that each operator’s tower group has internal connectivity while keeping overall deployment cost as small as possible, with no obligation to connect distinct operator groups.

As the campus facilities coordinator, decide which walkways and bridges to construct so that each group of buildings forms an internal network for pedestrian access with minimum total construction cost, and building groups may remain isolated from each other.
As the logistics planner, pick which private roads to secure so that each cluster of warehouses can reach one another with the least total cost outlay, and clusters are allowed to be independent.

As the wildlife corridor designer, select which habitat linkages to preserve or create so that all endangered sites in each conservation group are mutually reachable, minimizing total land or restoration cost, and different conservation groups do not need to connect.

As the festival organizer, decide which temporary walkways and bridges to install so that all attractions in each program area are connected for visitors while minimizing the total material and labor cost, and separate program areas can remain unlinked.

As the campus security chief, choose which surveillance cables to lay so that every cluster of cameras is connected to its local hub with the smallest possible total cabling cost, and hubs for different clusters do not have to be joined.

As the emergency response coordinator, pick which access routes to clear so that each set of critical sites is connected for team movement, minimizing the total effort or expense, and different sets can remain disconnected from one another.

As the theme park operations manager, determine which service roads to maintain so that all rides in each operational zone are accessible to maintenance crews while keeping upkeep cost minimal, and operational zones need not be connected.

As the agricultural cooperative planner, select which farm tracks to upgrade so that every group of member farms is mutually reachable for equipment sharing with minimal total upgrade cost, and separate member groups may stay separate.

As the smart city engineer, choose which sensor links to install so that sensors in each monitoring cluster form a connected network while minimizing the total installation budget, and monitoring clusters do not have to be interconnected.

As the water authority, decide which distribution mains to reinforce so that all endpoints in each service area are connected to each other, minimizing the sum of reinforcement costs, and different service areas can remain independent.

As the national park manager, pick which ranger trails to keep open so that every patrol points group is connected for movement between points with the least total maintenance effort, and patrol groups are not required to be linked.

As the retail rollout coordinator, choose which delivery routes to establish so that stores in each territory can be reached from one another while minimizing total distance or cost, and different territories do not need to be connected.

As the research station lead, decide which supply links to set up so that instruments in each experiment cluster can exchange materials internally at minimum total setup cost, and separate experiment clusters may remain disconnected.
Plan which streets to pave to link all homes in each residential cluster while keeping total paving cost as low as possible, and there is no need to join different clusters together.
Choose which trails to maintain so that shelters inside every park sector are reachable from each other while keeping total maintenance effort minimal, and different sectors do not have to be joined.
Pick walkways to erect so that booths within each vendor area are connected for foot traffic while spending as little on construction as possible, and vendor areas can be independent.

Determine which microwave links to install so that antenna sites belonging to each service zone form an internal network while minimizing overall installation expense, and service zones need not be linked.

Select roads to sign as delivery routes so that depots in each service region are mutually reachable while minimizing total distance covered by the chosen routes, with different regions allowed to remain separate.

Choose pipe segments to lay so that all customer clusters in each pressure zone are connected within that zone while minimizing the summed cost of pipe installation, and pressure zones do not have to connect to each other.

Decide which access lanes to keep clear so that hydrants within every fire district are connected by a passable path while keeping the total clearance effort minimal, and separate districts need not be connected.
Pick which cabling segments to run so that computers in each lab pod are mutually connected while using the smallest possible amount of cable, and lab pods may remain isolated from each other.

Determine which signage corridors to build so that stores in each shopping cluster are linked internally for customer flow while minimizing construction outlay, and shopping clusters do not need to be joined.

Select lift corridors and walkways to ensure that lodges and facilities within each valley area are connected for guest movement while keeping the total development cost low, with valleys not required to have links between them.
Decide which footpaths to keep open so that campsites in each loop can reach each other on maintained paths while minimizing total trail upkeep cost, and different loops can be unconnected.

Select shuttle paths on the apron so that gates assigned to each terminal cluster are connected by service routes while minimizing total travel distance of the routes, and terminal clusters do not have to be linked.

Pick corridor segments to renovate so that wards grouped for certain services are internally accessible while keeping the overall renovation cost as small as possible, and different service groups need not be connected.

Decide where to build small sea walls and access tracks so that sets of fish processing sites along each stretch are linked for transport while minimizing combined construction cost, and stretches may remain independent.

Select which gravel roads to grade so that all plots in each varietal block are connected for machinery movement while minimizing the total grading expense, with different varietal blocks not required to have connections between them.

Choose which temporary bridges to deploy so that critical points within each rescue sector are mutually reachable while minimizing the total deployment cost, and separate sectors can stay disconnected.

Determine which transport links to fund so that patient pickup locations in each service cluster form an internal network while keeping total funding outlay minimal, and clusters do not have to be connected to each other.

As the network administrator, choose which existing links to enable so that servers within every subnet are mutually reachable through enabled links while minimizing the overall link activation cost, and different subnets need not be connected.

As the emergency services planner, determine which pathways to clear so that all clinics inside every response zone are connected by cleared routes with the least total clearance effort, and there is no requirement to link zones together.

As the water authority engineer, choose pipeline segments to lay so that reservoirs in each water district are connected while minimizing the overall piping cost, and districts do not have to be connected with each other.

As the rural internet project lead, pick which wireless hops to activate so that community access points within each village network are connected while minimizing the sum of setup and operating costs, and connecting different village networks is not required.

As the shipping route planner, decide which maritime lanes to reserve so that terminals in each shipping alliance are reachable from one another while minimizing combined reservation fees, and separate alliances do not have to be connected.

As the security systems engineer, choose which camera links to enable so that sensors in each secured sector form a connected monitoring network while minimizing the sum of link costs, and different secured sectors may remain disconnected.

As the regional airline scheduler, choose flight legs to operate so that airports in each partnership region are connected by operated legs while aiming to minimize the total operating cost, and different partnership regions do not have to be joined.

As the cold chain logistics manager, decide which refrigerated links to establish so that cold storage facilities in each distribution cluster are connected while keeping the total link cost as low as possible, and clusters do not have to be joined.

As the gas network coordinator, pick which feeder pipes to commission so that delivery points in every service segment are connected while minimizing total commissioning cost, and service segments do not need to be linked.

As the festival infrastructure manager, choose which supply conduits to install so that vendors in each themed zone are connected to utilities while minimizing combined installation expense, and themed zones may remain separate.

As the ad hoc network researcher, decide which radio links to establish so that nodes in each experiment group form a connected mesh while minimizing total energy and setup cost, and different experiment groups do not need to be connected.

A city planner asks to connect neighborhoods' bus stops with as little new pavement as possible so that stops belonging to the same service area are linked by continuous bus lanes while different service areas may remain separate.

A network engineer asks to lay optical cable between buildings minimizing total trench length while ensuring that outlets that belong to the same department are all reachable through the installed cable but different departments can stay isolated.
A museum curator asks to run decorative piping minimizing installation cost so that exhibits in the same thematic collection are joined by the piping while different collections can be independent.
A park manager must create footpaths minimizing the total cleared distance so that all benches in the same picnic area are connected by paths while picnic areas do not have to connect to each other.

A telecom operator needs to activate wireless relays minimizing cumulative operational cost so that relays serving the same customer group can communicate via active links while relays for different customer groups may stay separate.

A campus planner wants to install bike routes minimizing paving costs so that building groups used by the same faculty are internally connected by the new routes while different faculties' zones may stay disconnected.
A homeowner wishes to lay garden stepping stones minimizing material cost so that plants in each themed bed are connected by a continuous stone route while different beds can remain separate.

An IT administrator is selecting which server links to enable to keep total latency cost low while guaranteeing that machines used by the same application can communicate through enabled links but different applications do not require interconnection.

A contractor must choose which segments of a proposed sewer network to install to minimize installation cost while ensuring that all residences served by the same septic cluster are joined by installed pipes and clusters may stay unconnected.

A wildlife manager needs to open animal trails minimizing total trail length so that observation points for each monitoring project are joined by trails while projects are independently connected and need not interlink.

A shipping coordinator wants to pick which river routes to use to minimize fuel and toll expenses while ensuring that docks within each regional trading group are connected by chosen routes but different trading groups can remain separate.

A school administrator is planning playground connectors minimizing construction expense so that equipment pieces in the same activity zone are joined by safe connectors while activity zones do not have to connect to other zones.

A retail chain planner chooses which delivery lanes to contract to minimize total contracted cost while making sure shops in each merchandising cluster are interconnected via the contracted lanes and clusters can be disconnected from each other.

A facility manager decides which hallway links to keep lit to minimize energy cost while ensuring that rooms assigned to the same department remain connected by lit hallways and departments do not need mutual connectivity.
An urban gardener arranges irrigation tubing minimizing total tubing length so that planter boxes in each vegetable bed are connected by tubes while separate beds can remain unconnected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of intersections or distinct map points (nodes) on the city map — the count of locations that roads connect and that are referenced by terminal groups and road segments.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct road segments (edges) available for upgrading on the map — each entry represents one stretch of roadway between two intersections.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of neighborhood clusters, each being a set of intersection identifiers that represent homes/locations which must be connected to one another by upgraded roads. Clusters are independent (clusters do not need interconnection).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint intersection of a particular road segment — one end of the candidate road to upgrade.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint intersection of the same road segment — the opposite end of that candidate road to upgrade.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary cost to upgrade that road segment (between intersection_u and intersection_v). When selecting roads to upgrade, these costs are summed to compute the total construction bill.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct office sites in the network (the number of nodes). Node identifiers in the link list range from 1 to this number and are used to reference which offices a candidate fiber stretch connects.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available fiber stretches (edges) that can be activated. This tells you how many link entries to expect in the link list.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of office-site groups. Each element is a set of site identifiers that must be connected among themselves by activated fiber. Different groups are independent — there is no requirement to connect groups to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint site ID of this candidate fiber stretch. Together with 'v' identifies the two offices the link would directly join if activated.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint site ID of this candidate fiber stretch. The pair (u, v) specifies an undirected fiber link between those two office sites.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Cost (weight) to activate this fiber stretch. If you choose to include this link in the final plan you pay this cost once; the total objective is the sum of costs for all activated links (shared links are paid once).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct locations in the park sketch (trailheads, junctions, or points where paths can meet). Node IDs in the instance range over these locations and are used as endpoints for possible footpaths.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of proposed footpath segments in the sketch. Each listed segment is a candidate path the superintendent may choose to pave; selecting a segment incurs its listed paving length.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups of trailhead location IDs. For each group, every trailhead in that group must be mutually reachable along chosen paved paths. Different groups do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The ID of one endpoint location for this proposed footpath segment (refers to a trail location/node in the sketch).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The ID of the other endpoint location for this proposed footpath segment (the segment connects this location to the one named by 'u').

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The paving length (cost) of this footpath segment connecting u and v. The superintendent sums these lengths for all chosen segments; the goal is to minimize the total while ensuring each trailhead group is internally connected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of substations (nodes) on the map. Substations are the labeled locations planners can connect with transmission lines; these labels are referenced by the edge list and by each neighborhood group.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate transmission lines (edges) shown on the map. Each line appears exactly once in the edge list with its two endpoint substations and installation cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A collection of neighborhoods (groups). Each neighborhood is a list of substation identifiers that must be internally connected by the chosen transmission lines; different neighborhoods are allowed to remain disconnected from one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint substation identifier for this candidate transmission line. Matches a node label from the total_substations set.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint substation identifier for this candidate transmission line. Matches a node label from the total_substations set.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The installation (paving) cost for this transmission line. When selecting lines to connect each neighborhood, sum these costs for the chosen lines; the objective is to minimize that sum.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of rooms or exhibit locations in the museum floor plan; each node id from 1..num_rooms identifies a distinct room that can hold exhibits or corridors.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential corridors or connecting doors drawn on the plan; each corresponds to a possible hallway the curator can repair to connect rooms.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of themed clusters where each cluster is a set of room ids containing exhibits of the same theme; the curator must ensure that, for every cluster, all rooms in that cluster become mutually reachable by repaired corridors (clusters do not need to be connected to each other).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint room id of a potential corridor: the first room that corridor connects on the floor plan.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint room id of a potential corridor: the second room that corridor connects on the floor plan.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Renovation cost to open or repair the corridor between room_u and room_v; the curator's objective is to minimize the total sum of chosen repair_costs while ensuring each themed cluster is internally connected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct agricultural plots (graph nodes) in the area; each plot is a location where canals can start, end, or meet.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate canal segments (graph edges) that could be dug between pairs of plots; each represents a possible connection you may choose to build.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups of plots that each farmer wants connected by canals; for every group, the chosen set of dug canals must make those plots mutually reachable, while groups may remain disconnected from one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint plot identifier for a candidate canal segment; this is one of the two plots the segment would connect if dug.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint plot identifier for the candidate canal segment; together with plot_u it specifies which two plots the segment would join.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The digging cost (length) of that candidate canal segment between plot_u and plot_v; adding this segment to the plan increases total digging by this amount.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct tower locations (graph nodes) in the planning area — i.e., how many possible tower endpoints exist for backhaul links.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate backhaul links (graph edges) under consideration — each represents a possible build between two tower sites with a listed cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups where each group is the set of tower site IDs belonging to a single mobile operator; every group must be internally connected by chosen links, but groups do not need to connect to one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint tower site ID of this candidate backhaul link — the first tower the link would connect if built.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint tower site ID of this candidate backhaul link — the second tower the link would connect if built.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to build this candidate backhaul link between the two endpoints; the solver sums costs of chosen links to minimize total deployment expense.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of nodes on the campus map — each node denotes a building, courtyard, or pathway junction that can be an endpoint for a walkway or bridge.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate connecting pieces (walkways and little bridges) under consideration; each corresponds to one potential construction project linking two nodes.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups (islands) of building node IDs. For each group, every building listed must be connected to the others in that same group by the chosen construction pieces; groups are allowed to remain isolated from one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node ID for a candidate walkway/bridge — the starting building or junction that this construction piece would attach to.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node ID for the candidate walkway/bridge — the destination building or junction that this construction piece would attach to.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost (weight) to build that specific walkway or bridge between the two endpoint nodes; used to compute the total construction bill to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct locations in the private-road network (warehouses and any intermediate junctions). Nodes are referenced by their integer IDs (e.g., 1..num_nodes) and these IDs are used in road endpoint fields and in the cluster lists.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate private roads that can be secured. Each corresponds to one undirected connection between two locations and appears once in the list of roads; selecting a road means paying its cost once.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of clusters (groups) of warehouse node IDs. For each cluster, the secured roads chosen must connect every warehouse in that cluster (clusters may remain disconnected from each other). Each group is an array of node IDs drawn from the total_locations.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location ID of a candidate private road. This integer refers to a node in the network (1..total_locations). Roads are undirected, so location_u is a label for one end of the road.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location ID of the candidate private road. Together with location_u it identifies the undirected road connecting two locations in the network.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to secure (pay for) that private road between location_u and location_v. If the road is chosen, this amount is added once to the total bill used to evaluate solutions.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of habitat patches (graph nodes) in the landscape map, including endangered sites and intermediate patches that can be used to route corridors.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential or existing habitat linkages (graph edges) between patches that can be preserved or created; each represents a corridor whose cost is listed separately.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups of endangered sites (node IDs). For each group, every site in that group must be mutually reachable using the selected corridors; different groups do not need to be connected to one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint patch ID of a potential corridor — identifies one habitat patch that the corridor would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint patch ID of the same potential corridor — identifies the second habitat patch the corridor would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost (land acquisition or restoration) to preserve or create the corridor between the two patches; if that corridor is chosen its cost is added once to the total.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct locations on the festival map (each attraction or intersection where a temporary walkway or bridge can meet). Use this to understand the range of node IDs used throughout the instance.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate temporary walkways or bridges under consideration. Each corresponds to one possible connection between two locations with an associated installation cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups, each listing the location IDs of attractions that belong to the same program area. All locations in each program area must be connected by the selected walkways/bridges; different program areas may remain disconnected.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The ID of one endpoint location for this candidate walkway/bridge (an attraction or intersection). This together with 'v' identifies which two places the path would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The ID of the other endpoint location for this candidate walkway/bridge. The edge connects endpoint_a and endpoint_b (undirected): installing it allows movement both ways between these two locations.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The material and labor cost to install this walkway/bridge between the two endpoints. When selecting edges, sum these costs to compute the total festival spending to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct campus locations (junctions, camera positions, or hub sites) that can appear as endpoints for surveillance cable runs. Node IDs in the instance range from 1..total_campus_locations.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of candidate cable runs (undirected connections) between campus locations. Each run is a potential installation option with an associated installation cost; you may choose a subset to install.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of camera clusters where each cluster is a set of location IDs (cameras and, if specified, the local hub) that must be connected to one another by installed cables. Different clusters do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location ID for a candidate cable run — the first campus site the cable would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location ID for the candidate cable run — the second campus site the cable would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The cost (length/price) to install the cable between the two endpoints. When evaluating plans, add each installed run's installation_cost once to get the total cabling cost to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations represented in the road network (this includes all critical facilities and any intermediate junctions). Use this to know how many node identifiers exist in the scenario.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate access routes (roads) in the network that could be cleared. Each corresponds to one potential edge connecting two locations.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups of critical facilities (each group is a list of site/node identifiers). For each listed group, the cleared roads must connect every site in that group internally; groups do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location (node identifier) of a candidate road that could be cleared. Paired with 'v' it defines which two sites the road connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location (node identifier) of the candidate road. Together with 'u' it identifies the two locations joined by this route.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The effort or expense required to clear this specific road (edge). When selecting roads to connect each critical_site_group, sum these clearing_cost values for chosen roads to compute the plan's total cost (do not double-count the same road).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct park locations represented in the graph (rides, maintenance depots, and service intersections). These are the vertices the solver indexes when choosing which service roads to keep.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate service roads in the map. Each corresponds to an edge the operations team can decide to maintain (pay upkeep for) or drop.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups of location indices, where each group lists the rides/locations belonging to one maintenance (operational) zone. The chosen maintained roads must make the locations inside each listed zone mutually reachable by maintenance crews; different zones do not need to be connected to one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location index of a candidate service road. Together with 'road_endpoint_b' this identifies which two park locations the road would connect if maintained.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location index of the candidate service road connecting this node to 'road_endpoint_a'.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The annual upkeep cost (weight) of maintaining this specific service road. In the objective, each chosen road's upkeep_cost is added once; the solver seeks the set of roads of minimal total upkeep that connects every operational zone internally.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of farms (graph nodes) in the cooperative map. Each farm is a node ID that may appear in terminal groups; this tells a solver the size of the farm set to consider when choosing tracks to upgrade.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate farm tracks (graph edges) that could be upgraded. Each represents a possible bidirectional route between two farms that incurs an upgrade fee if selected.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups of farm IDs where each group is a neighborhood of member farms that must be mutually reachable along upgraded tracks. Different groups may remain disconnected from each other if that reduces total upgrade cost.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The integer ID of one endpoint farm for this candidate track. Together with 'v' it identifies which two farms the track would connect if upgraded.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The integer ID of the other endpoint farm for this candidate track. The track is considered bidirectional for equipment movement between farm_node_u and farm_node_v.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to upgrade this particular track between the two endpoint farms. If the plan selects this track, its upgrade_fee is added once to the total cost the solver seeks to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of sensor nodes in the city network (each node is a distinct sensor identified by an index). This tells you how many sensors exist that can be connected by links.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available sensor links (candidate connections) you can choose to install. Each entry corresponds to one possible physical/wireless link between two sensors.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of monitoring clusters (groups of sensor IDs). For each cluster, the chosen links must connect all sensors in that cluster internally; clusters do not have to be connected to one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint sensor ID of a candidate link (an integer index identifying a specific sensor).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint sensor ID of the same candidate link (an integer index identifying a specific sensor).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Installation cost (weight) of the candidate link between the two endpoint sensors. Costs are additive and you pay each chosen link once; the goal is to minimize the total of these costs while connecting all sensors within each cluster.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of pipe junctions and endpoints in the city's water network graph; these are the node identifiers planners use when deciding which mains to reinforce.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distribution mains (edges) in the network that are candidates for reinforcement; each corresponds to a potential reinforced pipe segment connecting two endpoints.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of service areas, where each service area is a set of endpoint node IDs. For each service area, every endpoint listed must be connected to the others in that same area by reinforced mains in the final plan; different service areas may remain disconnected from one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node identifier of this distribution main (one end of the pipe segment).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node identifier of this distribution main (the other end of the pipe segment).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The cost to reinforce this mains segment; if planners include this pipe in their solution, its numeric cost contributes to the total reinforcement cost to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct park points (nodes) on the map — each is a lookout, supply or patrol point referenced by an index; all trail endpoints use these node indices.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate trails (edges) on the map that can be kept open; each trail connects two nodes and represents a possible maintenance cost to include in the plan.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of patrol-point groups, where each group is a list of node indices that must be internally connected by the kept trails (so every point in the same patrol group can reach every other); different patrol groups do not need to be connected to one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node index of a candidate trail; refers to a park point (see total_nodes).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node index of the candidate trail; paired with trail_endpoint_u to identify which two park points the trail connects.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The upkeep cost to keep this trail open (weight of the edge). If the trail is selected in the plan, this cost is counted once toward the total maintenance effort.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of store locations (graph nodes) in the rollout. Stores are numbered 1..num_nodes and these IDs are used when listing candidate routes and territory memberships.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate delivery routes (graph edges) available to open. Each route entry describes one possible undirected connection between two stores that the planner may choose.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of territories; each territory is a list of store node IDs that must be internally connected by the selected routes. Territories remain separate from one another and do not need connections between groups.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The store node ID at one end of this candidate route. Together with 'v' identifies the two stores that this undirected route would connect if opened.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The store node ID at the other end of this candidate route. Together with 'u' identifies the two stores that this undirected route would connect if opened.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Numeric cost (for example distance in km or monetary cost) to open and use this route between the two stores. The objective is to minimize the sum of route_cost for all routes chosen to connect all stores inside each territory.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of instrument locations (nodes) in the station diagram — every instrument or junction that can be connected by supply links.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of possible supply links shown in the diagram — each candidate pipe or cable that could be installed between two instrument locations.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: Lists of instruments that belong to the same experiment cluster. For each listed cluster, the installed links must make those instruments mutually reachable (internally connected); different clusters may remain disconnected from one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint instrument or junction of a candidate supply link (one end of the pipe/cable). Matches a node index from the station diagram.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint instrument or junction of the candidate supply link (the opposite end of the pipe/cable). Matches a node index from the station diagram.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary or resource cost to install that particular supply link between the two endpoints (u and v). The optimization sums chosen links' installation_costs to produce the minimum total setup cost while connecting each experiment_cluster internally.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct locations in the road network (homes and any street intersections or endpoints). Node IDs range from 1..total_locations and identify where streets meet or where homes sit.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate street segments that could be paved. Each street is a connection between two locations and has a listed paving cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of residential clusters. Each cluster is a list of node IDs corresponding to homes that must be connected to each other by paved streets; different clusters do not need to be joined.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The node ID of one endpoint of this candidate street segment (a location where the street meets another street or a home).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The node ID of the other endpoint of this candidate street segment.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to pave this street segment. The planner seeks a set of streets whose total paving_cost sum is minimal while ensuring every home in each residential cluster is connected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of shelter locations (graph nodes) in the park that can be connected by maintained trails.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of existing trails (graph edges) between shelter locations that are candidates for maintenance.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of park sectors; each sector is a set of shelter identifiers that must be connected to one another by maintained trails (sectors do not need to be connected to other sectors).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint shelter for this trail — a node at one end of the candidate trail to be (optionally) maintained.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint shelter for this trail — the node at the opposite end of the candidate trail.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The maintenance effort (weight/cost) required to repair or maintain this trail between the two shelters; if chosen, its cost contributes once to the total maintenance effort.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct locations on the market map — this includes individual booths and any intersection or junction points that can be used when planning walkways. Every node index used in edges refers to one of these locations.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate walkways (undirected connections) surveyed for construction. Each potential walkway is a possible edge between two locations that can be built at the listed cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups where each group lists the locations (booth indices) that belong to the same vendor area. For the final layout every location in each vendor_area must be connected to the others in that same group by chosen walkways; different vendor_areas do not have to be connected together.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location index of a potential walkway — refers to a specific booth or junction (using the node numbering from num_locations).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location index of the same potential walkway — together with walkway_end_a defines an undirected candidate edge between two locations.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary cost to build the potential walkway between the two endpoints (walkway_end_a and walkway_end_b). When evaluating layouts, sum the construction_cost of each chosen walkway (do not double-count any walkway used by multiple vendor areas).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of antenna sites (graph nodes) in the planning sketch. Each site ID identifies a tower that can be connected by microwave links.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential microwave links (graph edges) considered for installation. Each entry represents one possible link between two antenna sites.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: The service zones: a list of groups where each group contains the antenna site IDs that must be connected internally. Zones are independent — groups do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint antenna site ID of a candidate microwave link (one node of the edge).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint antenna site ID of the candidate microwave link (the other node of the edge).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Installation cost (weight) for the microwave link between the two endpoints u and v. The solver sums chosen link_install_cost values to compute total installation expense; each chosen link is counted once.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of locations (nodes) in the road network — this counts every junction and depot included in the map. Node IDs in edges and terminal groups refer to these locations.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate roads (edges) in the network that planners may choose to sign as delivery routes. Each road is a possible selection contributing its distance to the overall signed-route length.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups where each group is the set of depot node IDs belonging to one service region. For each group, the chosen signed roads must make all depots in that region mutually reachable; different groups may remain disconnected from one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The ID of one endpoint location of a candidate road. This refers to a node in the network (a depot or an intersection).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The ID of the other endpoint location of the candidate road. Together with road_endpoint_u it identifies which two locations the road connects.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length or cost of that candidate road. If this road is selected to be signed, its distance is added to the total signed-route distance that the planners are minimizing.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of junctions (nodes) in the town plan — every customer cluster, intersection, or valve location that can serve as an endpoint for a pipe segment is represented by one of these nodes. This count defines the set of node indices used elsewhere.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential pipe segments (edges) that can be installed. Each segment is a candidate connection between two junctions and has a specified installation cost; the solver chooses a subset of these segments.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups, one per pressure zone, where each group contains the node indices of customer clusters that must be connected within that pressure zone. Different groups (pressure zones) do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The node index of one endpoint junction for this potential pipe segment. Together with 'v' it identifies which two junctions the segment would connect if installed.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The node index of the other endpoint junction for this potential pipe segment. Used with 'u' to locate the segment between two junctions.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to install this pipe segment between the given endpoints. The solver minimizes the sum of installation_cost over all chosen segments; each installed segment is counted once.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of graph nodes representing street intersections or specific locations where hydrants may sit. All node IDs used elsewhere (u, v, and terminal lists) refer to this numbering.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate access lanes (graph edges) that can be cleared. Each lane connects two nodes (intersections) and has a clearance cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups, one per fire district; each group is a list of node IDs that host hydrants in that district. For each group, the chosen set of cleared lanes must provide a passable path between every pair of node IDs in that group. Different groups do not need to be connected to one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node ID of a candidate lane (an intersection or hydrant location). Matches the node numbering used in num_intersections_and_hydrant_locations and in fire_district_hydrant_groups.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node ID of the candidate lane. Lanes are undirected: choosing this lane makes travel possible both ways between lane_endpoint_u and lane_endpoint_v.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The effort (cost) required to clear this lane so it is passable. The total plan cost is the sum of clearance_cost values for all lanes selected; choose lanes so every district's hydrants are connected at minimum total clearance_cost.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct computers or connection points marked on the floor plan; every machine is a node that must be accounted for when deciding which cable runs to pull.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of possible cable segments shown on the plan — each is a candidate run you can choose to pull cable along to connect machines.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of lab pods, where each pod is a group of machine node IDs that must be internally connected by the chosen runs. Different pods may remain isolated from each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint machine/location ID of a candidate cable run (one end of the segment on the floor plan).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint machine/location ID of the candidate cable run (the opposite end of the segment on the floor plan).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (amount of cable) required to install this run. When choosing runs, add each chosen run's length once; the objective is to minimize the total cable length while ensuring every pod is internally connected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct points on the shopping-centre map (these are store entrances or corridor junctions). Nodes are referenced by integer IDs used throughout the instance.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate corridor segments shown on the map. Each potential corridor is an edge that can be built to link two points (stores or junctions) and has an associated build cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of shopping clusters: each group is a list of node IDs corresponding to stores that must be connected to one another by the built corridors. Each cluster must be internally connected; clusters do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node ID of the candidate corridor (an integer referring to a store or junction on the map). Corridors are undirected, so this is one of the two endpoints.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node ID of the candidate corridor (an integer referring to a store or junction). Together with 'corridor_endpoint_u' it identifies the corridor segment.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to build that corridor segment between the two endpoints. If the corridor is selected in the plan, this cost is added once to the total construction outlay; costs are nonnegative.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct resort sites (lodges, facilities, or corridor junctions) modeled as graph nodes; node identifiers reference these sites when defining corridors and terminal lists.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate connections (lift corridors or pedestrian walkways) that could be built; each corresponds to one possible edge between two sites with an associated construction cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of valley areas, where each group is a list of site node IDs (lodges and facilities) that must be connected to one another inside that valley; different groups (valleys) do not need connections between them.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one endpoint site for this candidate corridor (a lodge, facility, or junction).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other endpoint site for this candidate corridor; together with 'u' it specifies which two sites the corridor would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The development cost to build the corridor between the two endpoint sites; the solver sums costs of chosen corridors to minimize total spending (each built corridor counted once).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations in the park model (campsites and trail intersections). Nodes are the identifiers used for endpoints of footpaths.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate footpath segments (trail edges) under consideration for continued maintenance. Each corresponds to one undirected edge between two locations.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of loops; each element is a set of location IDs representing the campsites that belong to one weekend loop. For each group, the maintained footpaths chosen must connect all listed campsites, but different groups may remain disconnected.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint location (a campsite or intersection) of this footpath segment.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint location (a campsite or intersection) of this footpath segment.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Annual maintenance cost for keeping this footpath segment open. The solver sums these costs for all kept segments and seeks the minimum total while satisfying connectivity requirements for each loop.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of distinct gate locations and apron junctions (graph nodes) where shuttle routes can start, end, or intersect. Node IDs referenced elsewhere range from 1..this number.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate service-lane segments (graph edges) that can be chosen to form shuttle routes between gates/junctions. Each represents a drivable apron segment between two nodes.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of terminal clusters: each element is a set/list of gate node IDs that must be mutually connected by the chosen service segments. Clusters are independent — they do not need to be connected to other clusters.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node ID (a gate or junction) of this candidate service-lane segment. Matches a node index in total_gates_and_junctions.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node ID of this candidate service-lane segment. Together with segment_endpoint_u defines which two gates/junctions the segment links.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The driving distance (cost) of this service-lane segment. When selecting segments to connect gates within each cluster, the solver sums these distances to minimize total shuttle travel; units are consistent across all segments.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations on the floorplan (wards, room junctions, or nodes). Each location is an endpoint for corridor segments.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of corridor segments that can be renovated. Each segment connects two locations and is a selectable item with an associated renovation cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of clinical-service groups; each group is a list of location identifiers (wards) that must be internally connected by renovated corridors. Different service groups do not have to be connected to one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location identifier of this corridor segment (node index for a ward or junction).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location identifier of this corridor segment.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Renovation cost for this corridor segment. If the segment is chosen its cost is added once to the total budget; choosing it creates an undirected connection between endpoint_a and endpoint_b.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct locations on the coastal map (fish-processing sites and any intermediate junction points). Each location is a graph node where a sea wall or access track can start, end, or meet.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate construction segments (small sea-wall pieces or access-track links) that could be built to connect two locations. Each corresponds to a graph edge.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups, each group listing the locations that belong to the same coastal stretch and therefore must be connected to one another by built structures. Different groups (stretches) may remain independent.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one endpoint location for this candidate construction segment (one end of the sea wall or access track).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other endpoint location for this candidate construction segment (the other end of the sea wall or access track).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to build this specific segment (sea wall piece or access track) between site_u and site_v. Total cost is the sum of chosen segments, counted once each.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of farm plots (graph nodes) in the layout; each node represents a distinct plot that tractors must travel to.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of existing gravel road segments (graph edges) that could be graded; each edge connects two plots and grading it incurs its listed cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of varietal blocks, each given as a group of plot identifiers; every plot in a block must be mutually reachable via chosen graded roads, but blocks do not need connections between them.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint plot of this gravel road segment; together with plot_id_v this defines which two plots the road connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint plot of this gravel road segment; roads are undirected so (plot_id_u, plot_id_v) is the same as (plot_id_v, plot_id_u).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Cost to grade this gravel road segment once (the expense added if this edge is selected); the solver sums chosen grading_costs to minimize total expense.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct checkpoints or sites on the exercise map (i.e., the number of nodes in the graph). These are the labeled locations where temporary bridges could connect and where rescue-sector checkpoints reside.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate temporary spans (bridges) available to deploy (i.e., the number of edges). Each represents a possible assembled span between two checkpoints with an associated deployment cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of rescue sectors; each sector is a group of checkpoint identifiers that must be mutually reachable by deployed spans. Different sectors are allowed to remain disconnected from one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint checkpoint identifier of a candidate temporary span (bridge). Matches a checkpoint label used in the map's node list.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint checkpoint identifier of the candidate temporary span (bridge). Together with span_endpoint_u it defines which two checkpoints the span would connect if deployed.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary or resource cost to deploy the span between span_endpoint_u and span_endpoint_v. The solver sums the costs of deployed spans to obtain the plan's total deployment cost.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pickup spots (nodes) in the transport network. Nodes are numbered consistently (e.g., 1..num_nodes) and every pickup spot must be included in the solution.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate transport links (edges) available for funding. Each entry describes one possible route connecting two pickup spots.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of service clusters; each cluster is a list of pickup-location IDs that must be internally connected by funded routes. Different clusters do not need to be connected to one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a candidate route, given as the pickup-location ID of a stop. Combined with 'v' it identifies the two stops that would be linked if this route is funded.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a candidate route, given as the pickup-location ID. The pair (u, v) denotes an undirected route between those two stops.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The cost to fund that specific route (u–v). Costs are nonnegative numbers; if a route is selected it contributes this amount once to the total funding outlay.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of servers in the network sketch; nodes are server identifiers used throughout the instance.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of physical links the crew sketched that can be enabled; each corresponds to a candidate connection between two servers.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: List of subnets, where each subnet is a list of server identifiers that must be mutually reachable via enabled links (subnets do not need to be connected to each other).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one server at an end of an existing link; together with 'v' it specifies which two servers the link connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other server at the end of an existing link; together with 'u' it specifies the link's two endpoints.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary cost to enable this existing link (counted once if the link is enabled); the optimizer sums these costs for chosen links.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations on the map (each indexed node represents a clinic or an intervening junction/location that can be used when clearing pathways).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate pathways (edges) between locations; each represents a route that can be cleared and has an associated clearance effort.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups, each group listing the indices of clinics that belong to the same emergency response zone — every clinic in a group must be connected to the others in that group by cleared pathways (zones do not need to be connected to each other).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Index of one endpoint location for this candidate pathway (one end of the undirected route that could be cleared).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Index of the other endpoint location for this candidate pathway (the opposite end of the undirected route that could be cleared).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Clearance effort (weight/cost) required to open this pathway between the two endpoints; if you choose to clear the route its cost is added once to the total.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of reservoir locations on the map; each reservoir corresponds to a graph node that can be connected by pipeline segments.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate pipeline segments (edges) available to install between reservoirs; each segment has an associated installation cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: List of water districts, where each district is a set of reservoir node IDs that must be internally connected by installed pipeline segments; districts do not need to be connected to one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint reservoir node ID for this candidate pipeline segment.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint reservoir node ID for this candidate pipeline segment.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Installation cost of this pipeline segment; this cost is added to the total only if the segment is selected to be laid.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of community access points (wireless nodes) in the entire deployment; nodes are the endpoints that can be connected by powered wireless hops and are indexed consistently in edges and terminal groups.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate wireless hops (undirected links) that can be activated; each corresponds to an available jump between two access points with an associated setup + operating cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups (each a list of node indices) where each group represents the access points belonging to one village; all access points in each listed village must be connected to one another in the chosen set of powered hops, while different villages do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (node index) of one endpoint access point for this potential wireless hop; pairs with 'v' to define which two access points the hop would join.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (node index) of the other endpoint access point for this potential wireless hop; together with 'u' specifies the two access points that would be connected if this hop is activated.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Total cost of activating this wireless hop (the sum of installation/setup cost and ongoing operating cost); when a hop is chosen it contributes this cost once to the overall objective, and hops should not be double-counted.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of maritime nodes in the planning graph (ports, terminals, or waypoint junctions). Nodes are the identifiers used when listing lanes and alliance terminals; the solver assumes nodes are numbered within this set.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate maritime lanes (graph edges) that can be reserved. Each lane connects two nodes and has an associated reservation fee.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A collection of shipping-alliance terminal groups. Each entry is a list of node IDs representing all terminals in one alliance; the final reserved lanes must ensure every terminal in the same alliance is reachable from every other member of that alliance (different alliances may remain separate).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The first endpoint node ID of this candidate maritime lane (one port or waypoint).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The second endpoint node ID of this candidate maritime lane (the other port or waypoint).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost (weight) to reserve this maritime lane. When selecting lanes to connect alliance terminals, the total objective is the sum of chosen lanes' reservation fees (each lane counted once).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of sensors (nodes) deployed in the facility map — the count of distinct sensor units that may be connected by camera links.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential camera links (edges) available between sensors in the map — each represents an enable-able connection with an associated cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: List of secured sectors, where each sector is a group (list) of sensor IDs that must be internally connected by enabled links. Sectors are independent and need not be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint sensor ID of a potential camera link; together with sensor_v identifies the two sensors the link would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint sensor ID of the potential camera link paired with sensor_u.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Cost to enable the camera link between sensor_u and sensor_v. When selecting links to connect sensors within each sector, sum these costs; each enabled link is counted once.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct airports in the regional network (graph nodes) that the scheduler may connect by operating flight legs.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of available direct flight routes (candidate legs) between airports; each corresponds to an edge the scheduler can choose to operate.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of partnership regions where each region is a list of airport identifiers. For each partnership region, the chosen operated legs must connect all airports in that region; different regions do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint airport for this candidate leg (one node of the edge). Used together with 'v' to specify which two airports the route connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint airport for this candidate leg (the other node of the edge). Together with 'u' it defines the direct route between two airports.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary cost to operate the flight leg between the two airports (u and v). The scheduler's objective is to select legs whose summed operating_costs are minimal while connecting all airports within each partnership region; each chosen leg's cost is counted once.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of cold storage facilities (warehouses) in the logistics network. Nodes are the facility identifiers (e.g. 1..n) that you can connect with refrigerated corridors.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of candidate refrigerated corridors (possible links) available in the network. Each corridor corresponds to one item in the edge list and is a candidate to be built at its given cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of distribution clusters, each given as a set/list of facility node IDs. For each cluster, the chosen refrigerated corridors must connect all facilities in that cluster internally. Different clusters do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint facility ID of a candidate refrigerated corridor. This references a facility node from the total_facilities set and pairs with facility_v to define the corridor.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint facility ID of a candidate refrigerated corridor. Combined with facility_u, it specifies which two facilities the corridor would link.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The cost to establish the refrigerated corridor between facility_u and facility_v. The solver will sum the costs of selected corridors; aim to minimize this total while ensuring each distribution_cluster is internally connected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct nodes in the gas network graph (junctions or delivery-point locations). Node IDs in the edge list and terminal groups refer to these nodes.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate feeder pipes available to commission (each pipe is an edge between two nodes). Each pipe has an associated commissioning cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of service segments; each element is a group (list) of node IDs that are delivery points inside that service area. For each group, the chosen set of commissioned pipes must connect all nodes in that group internally. Different groups do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node ID of a candidate feeder pipe (an endpoint junction or delivery point). Used together with 'v' to identify the pipe.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node ID of the candidate feeder pipe. Combined with 'u' this identifies which two network nodes the pipe would connect if commissioned.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The commissioning cost (weight) of the feeder pipe between nodes u and v. The optimization objective is to minimize the sum of these costs for the set of pipes chosen so that each service segment's delivery nodes become internally connected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations on the festival map (this includes vendor stalls, junctions, utility access points, or any numbered site). Node IDs in the instance range from 1..total_locations and are used to reference where conduits can start/end.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential conduit runs (edge candidates) between locations. Each run is a specific possible installation between two location IDs and has an associated installation cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
