global_fields.scenario_description: A list of themed vendor zones; each group is a set (or list) of location IDs representing all vendors in a theme that must be connected to each other by the installed conduits. Different themed groups may remain disconnected from one another in the final plan.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location ID for this potential conduit run (an integer referencing a site from 1..total_locations).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location ID for this potential conduit run. Together with location_a this defines which two sites the conduit would connect if installed.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The monetary cost to install the conduit between location_a and location_b. When selecting conduit runs for the festival plan, the sum of installation_cost for chosen runs is the value to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of wireless devices (graph nodes) in the deployment. Device IDs range over these nodes and are referenced by edges and terminal groups.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of candidate radio links (graph edges) available to establish between devices. Each represents a possible connection you may turn on at its associated cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of experiment groups, each given as a set of device IDs. For each group, the chosen links must make all devices in that group connected. Different experiment groups do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint device ID of this candidate radio link. Together with link_endpoint_b, this identifies which two devices would be connected if the link is enabled.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint device ID of this candidate radio link. The link connects link_endpoint_a and link_endpoint_b (undirected).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The cost of enabling this radio link: the one-time setup fee plus the ongoing energy cost (summed into a single weight). If the link is turned on it contributes this amount once to the total objective.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct bus stops (graph nodes) in the city layout. This counts every stop that can be used either as a required stop in a service area or as an intermediate junction (Steiner) when routing new lanes.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential road segments (graph edges) considered for laying new bus lanes. Each segment connects two stops and is a candidate to be paved; choosing a segment incurs its listed cost/length.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A collection of service-area groups, where each group is a list of bus stop identifiers that belong to the same transit service area. All stops in each listed group must be connected by chosen new lanes; different groups do not have to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint bus stop for this candidate road segment. Together with 'v' it defines which two stops the segment would connect if paved.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint bus stop for this candidate road segment. The pair (stop_u, stop_v) is the segment that can be chosen to join service-area stops.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The cost (e.g., length of new pavement) to build this road segment between stop_u and stop_v. If the segment is selected in the plan, this value contributes to the total pavement amount to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct node locations on the site plan (each node is a building or outlet location where fiber can be run to or through). Use this to confirm the node ID range for the plan.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential trench segments shown on the plan (each represents a possible cable run between two nodes). This counts the listed possible connections, not the chosen ones.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups, each group containing the node IDs for all outlets that belong to the same department. For each group, the installed trenches must connect every node in that group (different groups may remain disconnected from each other).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The node ID of one endpoint building/outlet for this potential trench segment.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The node ID of the other endpoint building/outlet for this potential trench segment.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of this trench segment — i.e., the length of cable/trench required between the two endpoints. The solver minimizes the sum of chosen segment lengths; overlapping segments count only once in the final total.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations in the museum layout represented as graph nodes — this includes exhibit positions and any intermediate pipe junctions; node indices in the input refer to these locations.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential pipe segments (graph edges) considered for installation; each edge connects two locations and is a candidate run of decorative piping.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of themed collections, each specified as a set of node indices corresponding to exhibits that must be connected by the installed piping (members of the same list element must be joined, different groups may remain separate).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location index of a candidate pipe segment — corresponds to a node ID for an exhibit position or junction.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location index of the candidate pipe segment — together with endpoint_a defines which two locations the pipe would join.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The cost (weight) to install that specific pipe segment between endpoint_a and endpoint_b, representing materials/labor for that run; the solver sums chosen installation_costs to minimize total expense.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations represented as nodes in the park layout. Each node is a bench location or a path junction used to index endpoints of candidate paths.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate path segments (undirected edges) between the locations. Each segment is a possible stretch of ground that can be cleared and counted toward the total cleared distance.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups, where each group is a list of node IDs corresponding to benches in the same picnic area. For each group, the final set of cleared paths must make those bench nodes reachable from one another (groups do not need to connect to other groups).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node ID of this candidate path segment (a bench or junction). Used together with 'v' to identify which two locations the segment would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node ID of this candidate path segment (a bench or junction). The segment connects endpoint_u and endpoint_v; edges are undirected so order does not matter.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The length (cost) of this path segment, in the unit used for the park (e.g., meters). If this segment is cleared it contributes this amount to the total cleared distance; the same physical segment cannot be counted twice.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of wireless relay sites (graph nodes) in the network map. Each relay is referenced by an index used elsewhere when specifying links and terminal groups.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential wireless links (graph edges) available for activation. Each link will be listed with its two endpoint relays and the operational cost to activate it.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of customer clusters where each cluster is represented by a list of relay indices. For each cluster, the selected active links must connect all relays in that cluster (clusters may remain disconnected from each other if cheaper).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint relay index of a potential wireless link; refers to a relay (node) from the total_relays set.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint relay index of the potential wireless link; paired with relay_u to identify the link between two relays.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The operational cost (weight) to activate the wireless link between relay_u and relay_v. The solver minimizes the sum of chosen activation_costs while ensuring every customer_cluster is internally connected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct campus locations (buildings or intersections) considered as nodes in the planning map; used to index and reason about all possible sites that bike routes might connect.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate bike-route segments (possible links between two campus locations) available for paving; each corresponds to one edge option whose cost can be chosen or omitted.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups where each group is the set of building node identifiers used by a single faculty; the planner must ensure that, for each group, the chosen paved links make every building in that faculty’s group reachable from every other building in the same group (groups may remain disconnected from one another).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one end of a candidate bike-route segment — corresponds to a specific campus building or intersection node.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other end of the candidate bike-route segment — the building or intersection node connected to endpoint_a by this link.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Cost to pave this specific candidate segment between endpoint_a and endpoint_b (monetary or relative units); the planner sums these costs for all chosen links and seeks the minimal total while satisfying the intra-faculty connectivity requirements.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct positions (plants or junction points) in the backyard layout — i.e., the count of nodes that stones can connect. Node identifiers in edges and terminal lists refer to these positions.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of candidate stone links that can be laid between two positions. Each corresponds to an edge in the graph with a given cost/length.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of themed garden beds; each entry is a group of node identifiers (plants) that must be connected by a continuous route of stepping stones. Different themed beds are allowed to remain disconnected from one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint position (plant or spot) of this candidate stone segment. Together with 'v' it defines which two positions the stone would join.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint position (plant or spot) of this candidate stone segment. The pair (u,v) marks the two positions a single stone piece would connect.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The cost or length of laying this single stone segment between its two endpoints (u and v). When evaluating layouts, sum the w values of chosen segments to get the total material/length cost to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct servers (nodes) in the rack/map the admin is deciding about. Node identifiers used elsewhere (e.g. in edges and terminal groups) refer to these servers.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of potential physical links between servers available to be switched on. Each of these corresponds to one edge in the topology with an associated latency cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups of server indices where each group represents the machines used by a single application. For each group, the admin must enable links so every server in that group can reach the others; different application groups do not need to be connected to one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint server index of a potential physical link (edge). This refers to a server id from the total_servers set.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint server index of the potential physical link. Pairs (server_endpoint_u, server_endpoint_v) define which two machines the link would connect if enabled.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The latency cost of enabling the physical link between the two endpoints. If the admin decides to switch this link on, this number is added once to the total latency cost; links are undirected and provide two-way connectivity.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations on the sewer map (junctions, house hookups, manholes). Node IDs range over these locations and are used as endpoints for proposed pipe segments.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of proposed pipe segments available for installation on the map. Each segment connects two nodes and can be chosen (installed) or not.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of groups where each group enumerates the node IDs of houses that belong to the same septic cluster. For each listed group, the chosen installed segments must connect all nodes in that group; different groups may remain disconnected from each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint node ID of a proposed pipe segment. Together with 'v' it identifies which two network locations the segment would join.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint node ID of a proposed pipe segment. The segment is between this node and 'u' (undirected connection).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary cost to install that pipe segment once. The contractor adds these costs for all chosen segments to compute the total installation bill; a segment chosen connects its endpoints for all relevant cluster connectivity.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct locations on the reserve map (these are nodes in the graph). Locations include observation points and any trail intersections that can be used to link observation points.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential trail segments between locations (these are edges in the graph). Each represents a candidate path the manager could open, with an associated length that would add to the total trail length if chosen.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: List of groups where each group is a set of location IDs that are observation points for a single monitoring project. All locations in a given group must be connected by opened trails, but different projects do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location ID of this potential trail segment. Together with 'v' it identifies the two locations the segment would connect.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location ID of this potential trail segment. The segment connects this location with the one named in 'u'. Trails are undirected (usable in either direction).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Length (cost) of the trail segment between the two endpoints, measured in the same distance units used for the reserve. Choosing this segment adds this length to the total trail length to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of docks (vertices) in the river network; these are the dock identifiers used elsewhere (in edge endpoints and terminal groups).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate river segments (edges) available to use; each represents a possible passage between two docks that can be selected and paid for.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of trading-region groups: each group is a list of dock identifiers that must be connected by the chosen routes. Different trading groups do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint dock identifier of this river segment (an integer referring to a dock listed among the num_docks).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint dock identifier of this river segment (an integer referring to a dock listed among the num_docks).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The combined fuel-plus-toll cost of using this river segment between dock_u and dock_v; if you select this segment for the solution, add this cost once to the total.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct playground locations or junctions (each corresponds to an equipment piece or a connector endpoint). Locations are referenced by integer IDs used throughout the connector list and zone definitions.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential connector pieces under consideration. Each entry represents a possible connector between two locations and will have an associated installation cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of activity zones; each zone is a group of location IDs (equipment pieces) that must be internally connected by installed connectors. Different activity zones do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint location ID of a potential connector — identifies the first playground location that this connector would join.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location ID of a potential connector — identifies the second playground location that this connector would join.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: The construction cost (weight) to install this connector between its two endpoints. The objective is to pick connectors minimizing the total installation_cost while ensuring each activity zone is connected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of shop locations (nodes) in the delivery network; each shop is a node ID used elsewhere to reference endpoints of lanes.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential delivery lanes (edges) available for contracting between shops in the network.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of merchandising clusters, each given as a list of shop IDs; for each cluster the contracted lanes must connect all shops inside that cluster, while different clusters may remain disconnected from one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint shop ID of a potential delivery lane; identifies one of the two shops that the lane would connect (undirected connection).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint shop ID of the same delivery lane; together with shop_a it specifies which pair of shops the lane connects.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Contracted cost for that delivery lane (edge) between shop_a and shop_b; if the lane is chosen the cost contributes once to the total contracted cost to be minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of rooms (graph nodes) in the building hallway network — the count of distinct rooms that may be connected by lit hallways.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of potential hallway links (graph edges) between rooms that the manager can choose to keep lit. Each link connects two rooms and has an associated energy cost.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: A list of departments where each department is given as a set/list of room identifiers. For each department, all listed rooms must be connected to one another by lit hallways in the final plan; different departments do not need to be connected to each other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint room of a hallway link (one node incident to the edge).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint room of the hallway link (the other node incident to the edge).

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Energy cost (weight) of keeping this hallway link lit. If the manager chooses this link, its cost is added once to the total energy sum being minimized.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct connection points in the irrigation layout (each node is a planter box, a junction, or another fixed point where tubing can join). This is the count of all graph vertices the gardener may use when planning tubing.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of candidate tubing segments (graph edges) considered in the plan. Each edge represents a possible straight run of hose between two connection points and is a candidate to be installed.

global_fields.name: terminal_groups
global_fields.scenario_description: Lists of node IDs that are planter boxes belonging to the same vegetable bed. Each listed group must be connected by installed tubing in the final plan; different groups (different beds) may remain disconnected from one another.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint connection point for a candidate tubing segment (one of the node IDs). In practice this is the first planter box or junction at the end of the segment.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint connection point for the candidate tubing segment (the second node ID). Together with 'endpoint_a' it defines the two ends of this possible hose run.

item_fields.name: w
item_fields.scenario_description: Cost of installing this tubing segment, expressed as the physical length of hose required (e.g., meters). The solver minimizes the sum of these lengths while ensuring each planter_bed_group is internally connected without redundant tubing.
